title: Integral closure and residue quotient of equal-constant pairs
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Put $P=k[[u]]\times k[[v]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $L=k((u))\times k((v))$ [def-weil-pbc-laurent-series], and $S=\{(f,g)\in P:f(0)=g(0)\}$, regarded as a subring of $L$. The integral closure of $S$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is exactly $P$. For $\epsilon=(1,0)\in P$ one has $P=S+S\epsilon=S[\epsilon]$ and $\epsilon^2=\epsilon$. The ring $S$ is local with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\{(f,g)\in S:f(0)=g(0)=0\}$ and residue map $c:S\to k$, $c(f,g)=f(0)=g(0)$. Give $k$ its $S$-module structure via $c$. The map $d:P\to k$, $d(f,g)=f(0)-g(0)$, is a surjective $S$-linear map with kernel $S$; hence it induces an $S$-linear isomorphism $P/S\cong k$. In particular $\mathfrak m(P/S)=0$ and $P/S$ is free of rank one over $S/\mathfrak m$, with basis the class of $\epsilon$.

proof.text: For $p=(f,g)\in P$ put $a=f(0)-g(0)\in k$, $\widetilde a=(a,a)\in S$ and $s=(f-a,g)\in S$. Then $p=s+\widetilde a\epsilon$. Since $\epsilon=(1,0)$ belongs to $P$ and $\epsilon^2=\epsilon$, this proves $P=S+S\epsilon=S[\epsilon]$. Moreover $(p-s)(p-s-\widetilde a)=\widetilde a^2\epsilon(\epsilon-1)=0$. Thus every $p\in P$ satisfies the monic polynomial $(T-s)(T-s-\widetilde a)\in S[T]$ and is integral over $S$.

proof.text:
Conversely let $z=(h_1,h_2)\in L$ satisfy $z^N+\sum_{i<N}s_i z^i=0$ with $N\ge1$ and $s_i\in S$. Project this equality to either Laurent coordinate $h$. All projected coefficients $b_i$ lie in $k[[t]]$. If $h
e0$ has lowest exponent $n<0$ and coefficient $b
e0$, the coefficient of $t^{Nn}$ in $h^N$ is $b^N
e0$: in the convolution product the only $N$ exponents at least $n$ summing to $Nn$ are all $n$. Every exponent occurring in $b_i h^i$ is at least $in>Nn$, so those terms have zero coefficient there. This contradicts the equation. Consequently each coordinate is zero or has no negative exponents, hence belongs to its power-series subring. Therefore $z\in P$, giving the reverse inclusion in the integral closure.

proof.text: Constant-coefficient evaluation is a ring homomorphism, since the degree-zero convolution has just the term $f(0)g(0)$. Thus $c:S\to k$ is a ring homomorphism, surjective via $a\mapsto(a,a)$, with kernel $\mathfrak m$. If $c(f,g)=a\ne0$, the cited power-series unit criterion over the local ring $k$ gives inverses $f^{-1},g^{-1}$; their constant coefficients are both $a^{-1}$, so $(f^{-1},g^{-1})\in S$. If $c(f,g)=0$, an inverse in $S$ would map to an inverse of zero in the nonzero field $k$, impossible. Finally any ideal properly containing $\mathfrak m$ contains such a unit, so $\mathfrak m$ is maximal; every proper ideal is contained in $\mathfrak m$ since its elements are nonunits. Hence it is the unique maximal ideal, and $c$ identifies $S/\mathfrak m$ with $k$.

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof of (1) implies (2), Case I and the subsequent by-hand delta calculation; explicit equal-constant algebra supplied by NE.

proof.text: The map $d$ is additive and for $s\in S$, $p=(f,g)\in P$ one has $d(sp)=c(s)f(0)-c(s)g(0)=c(s)d(p)$, proving $S$-linearity. Also $d(a,0)=a$ and $d(p)=0$ precisely when $p\in S$. Define the induced map $\bar d:P/S\to k$ by $[p]\mapsto d(p)$; replacing $p$ by $p+s$ leaves this value unchanged. Its inverse is $a\mapsto[(a,0)]$: the difference $p-(d(p),0)$ lies in $S$, and $d(a,0)=a$. For $s\in S$, $s(a,0)-(c(s)a,0)$ has both constant terms zero, so the inverse is also $S$-linear. For $s\in\mathfrak m$, $d(sp)=0$, whence $s[p]=0$. Under $S/\mathfrak m\cong k$, $[\epsilon]$ maps to $1$; explicitly $[p]=d(p)[\epsilon]$, uniquely since $\bar d([\epsilon])=1$. This is the asserted rank-one basis.

PowerSeries.constantCoeff p.2) ∧ Function.Surjective d ∧ LinearMap.ker d = Submodule.span S (S : Set (PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k)) ∧ (∃ e : ((PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k) ⧸ Submodule.span S (S : Set (PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k))) ≃ₗ[S] k, ∀ p : PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k, e (Submodule.Quotient.mk p) = d p) ∧ (∀ (s : S), s ∈ m → ∀ q : (PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k) ⧸ Submodule.span S (S : Set (PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k)), s • q = 0) ∧ ∃ (_ : Module (S ⧸ m) ((PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k) ⧸ Submodule.span S (S : Set (PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k)))), (∀ (s : S) (q : (PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k) ⧸ Submodule.span S (S : Set (PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k))), (Ideal.Quotient.mk m s) • q = s • q) ∧ ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin 1) (S ⧸ m) ((PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k) ⧸ Submodule.span S (S : Set (PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k))), b 0 = Submodule.Quotient.mk ((1, 0) : PowerSeries k × PowerSeries k)
lean.note: Integral closure is expressed elementwise by RingHom.IsIntegralElem for the canonical coordinatewise Laurent embedding; this is the defining predicate of integralClosure. The submodule in P/S is Submodule.span S (S : Set P), which equals S as a set. The scalar structures on k and P/S are existentially supplied with their exact residue-action formulas, not assumed.
